chunks: Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār asked him about the chickens of al-Ḥabash, so he said:
"It is not from the game; rather, birds are those that fly between the sky and the earth and spread their wings."

key_terms.السَّمَاءِ: the sky, part of the expression describing flight
key_terms.الصَّيْدِ: game animals or birds subject to hunting rulings
key_terms.الطَّيْرُ: birds, here in the legal sense being defined
key_terms.الْأَرْضِ: the earth, paired with the sky in defining the bird's movement
key_terms.الْحَبَشِ: Abyssinia/Ethiopia; describing the type of chickens mentioned
key_terms.دَجَاجِ: chickens or fowl being asked about in the ruling
key_terms.طَارَ: flew; indicating actual flight as part of the definition
key_terms.وَصَفَّ: spread its wings; part of the legal criterion mentioned

ai.seo_question: Are Ethiopian chickens considered game (ṣayd) in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal distinction regarding what is considered game (ṣayd). The Imam عليه السلام states that Ethiopian chickens are not counted as game, and defines game birds as those that fly between the sky and the earth and spread their wings.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2380 - Mu'awiya ibn Ammar asked him about Ethiopian chickens.
Imam (as) replied: "It is not considered part of the game (ṣayd); game birds are those that fly between the sky and the earth and flap their wings."
